findings: Document state is represented as a CRDT (e.g. Yjs/Automerge) so concurrent edits merge deterministically and commutatively with no data loss, avoiding any locking coordinator.
Clients apply edits optimistically and locally first (local-first architecture) and sync only small CRDT deltas afterward, so perceived latency stays sub-200ms independent of backend round-trips.
Each tenant/workspace is assigned an explicit data-residency region (US or EU) at creation, and that assignment pins where its document state, audit log, and processing compute physically run.

EU workspaces run on an entirely separate regional deployment (isolated cluster/account/network), not shared infra with row-level region tags, so residency is enforced at the infrastructure boundary rather than by application logic alone.

Collaboration sessions are always hosted in the workspace's home region; out-of-region collaborators connect across the network to that region's edge/gateway rather than the workspace's data ever leaving the region, trading extra network latency for the remote party instead of relocating data.
Real-time sync uses a region-local low-latency WebSocket/pub-sub relay carrying only CRDT deltas, with no cross-region dependency in the hot path, protecting the sub-200ms target.

Every accepted edit is appended to a per-region, multi-AZ durable append-only log (quorum-acknowledged, e.g. Kafka/Kinesis-style) before being confirmed committed, giving durability without any cross-region synchronous write.
The audit log is asynchronously exported to immutable/WORM object storage within the same region for tamper-evident long-term retention, decoupled from the low-latency edit path.
Regions operate autonomously with no cross-region synchronous dependency for editing or audit logging, so an outage in one region cannot stall or block the other.
On reconnect after a partition, queued local CRDT ops are replayed and re-logged idempotently (deduplicated via op IDs) so no buffered edit or audit event is silently dropped across a regional blip.
Presence/cursor signals are treated as ephemeral, best-effort data kept separate from the durable audit-log path, since only edit events carry the 'never lose an event' guarantee.
A single global database with row-level region tags was rejected as insufficient for the hard regulatory requirement, since logical tagging cannot guarantee physical data never crosses regions.
Synchronous cross-region audit-log writes/replication were rejected because they would either violate EU residency or create a stall/single point of failure during a network partition.
Operations monitor replication lag and audit-log backlog as leading indicators, with a defined degraded mode (e.g. local-buffer-only or read-only) for a regional outage instead of silent data loss.
